newsitem.title: FRANCE: PAL A330-300s to lift cargo capacity.
newsitem.headline: PAL A330-300s to lift cargo capacity.

text.p: The delivery of the first of eight new Airbus Industrie A330-300 airliners to Philippine Airlines will significantly increase the carrier's cargo capacity and help raise cargo revenue levels, PAL's executive vice president for administration and services, Manolo Aquino said.

Speaking to reporters after the signing ceremony here, Aquino said cargo currently contributes only around 12 percent of PAL's revenue but the new Airbus fleet should help raise that total closer to the industry average of between 20 and 40 percent.

"We are taking another big step in the rebuilding of PAL and are pinning our hopes on this aircraft which will be a regional workhorse for us. We feel it will make us very competitive and be able to carry much more cargo," Aquino said.
As part of a US$4 billion rebuilding programme, PAL is taking delivery of 28 Airbus aircraft in less than two years as well as eight new Boeing 747-400s.

The first revenue earning flight by PAL's 278 seat, twin-engined A330-300s will be on August 5 from Manila to Hong Kong replacing ageing Airbus A300B4 aircraft which will be returned to their lessor. The A330-300 can carry up to 33 standard belly cargo containers.
Airbus has already delivered the first two of four Airbus A340-300 268 seat, long-range airliners enabling PAL to fly non-stop from Manila to London. PAL also operates four A340-200s.
The first of 12 Airbus A320 airliners replacing PAL's Boeing 737 domestic fleet is due to be delivered next week.
PAL said it will be the first airline in the world to operate the A320,A330 and A340 at the same time offering significant standardisation benefits such as reduced pilot training and cross-crewing.
Airbus is a consortium comprising French-state owned Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc, Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA(Casa) of Spain.
